dervis-irab:15-18.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حملها): al-ḥiml with kasra is what is carried; the plural is aḥmāl and ḥumūla. Al-ḥiml is also the singular of al-ḥumūl, which are the howdahs or the camels carrying the howdahs. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "Al-ḥiml with kasra is what is carried on the back and the like; the plural is aḥmāl and ḥumūl. I carried (ḥamaltu) the goods, ḥamlan, of the pattern ḍaraba, so I am ḥāmil; and the feminine is ḥāmila with tāʾ because it is a shared adjective." And in al-Mukhtār: "Ibn al-Sikkīt said: al-ḥaml with fatḥa is what is in the belly or on the top of a tree, and al-ḥiml with kasra is what is on a back or a head. Al-Azharī said: this is the correct view and it is the saying of al-Aṣmaʿī. He said: a woman is ḥāmil or ḥāmila when she is pregnant. Whoever says ḥāmil says: this is an adjective that applies only to females; and whoever says ḥāmila builds it on 'she carried (ḥamalat), so she is ḥāmila'. Ibn Durayd mentioned that for the fruit-load of a tree there are two forms, with fatḥa and with kasra." Some scholar has composed a rule for this wondrous root, saying:
؎ ما كان في بطن فذاك حَمْلُ ∗∗∗ وإن على ظهر ورأس حِمْلُ
(What is in a belly is ḥaml; and what is on a back or a head is ḥiml.)
؎ والكفلاء والديات حُمْلُ ∗∗∗ جمع حِمال وحميل فادر
(And guarantors and blood-money payments are ḥuml, plural of ḥimāl and ḥamīl; so know it.)
؎ كثير حَمْل اسمه الحَمّال ∗∗∗ وحامل الديات والحِمّال
(One who carries much is called al-ḥammāl, as is one who bears blood-money payments, and al-ḥimmāl.)
؎ مصدر حمّلتك والحُمّال ∗∗∗ جمع لحامل لأي وِقر
(The verbal noun of "I burdened you (ḥammaltuka)"; and al-ḥummāl is a plural of ḥāmil for any load.)

* I'rab:
(يا أيها الناس أنتم الفقراء الى الله): (يا أيها الناس): its parsing has been given many times. (أنتم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (الفقراء) is the khabar (predicate). (الى الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (الفقراء), because it is the plural of faqīr, an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha).
(والله هو الغني الحميد): (الله) is a mubtadaʾ; (هو) is a second mubtadaʾ or a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); (الغني الحميد) is the khabar of inna (as the text has it) for the mubtadaʾ or for (هو); and the nominal sentence is the khabar of (الله).
(إن يشأ يذهبكم ويأتي بخلق جديد): (إن) is conditional; (يشأ) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (يذهبكم) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and its consequence; (ويأت) is conjoined to (يذهبكم); (بخلق) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يأت); (جديد) is an adjective (naʿt).
(وما ذلك على الله بعزيز): the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is the negative Ḥijāzī mā; (ذلك) is the subject (ism) of mā; (على الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (عزيز); the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾid) preposition; (عزيز) is genitive in form and accusative in position, being the khabar of mā.
(ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى): (لا) is negative; (تزر) is an imperfect verb; (وازرة) is the fāʿil (agent), or it is an adjective of an omitted agent, the implied form being "a bearing soul (nafs wāzira)"; (وزر) is the direct object (mafʿūl bihi); (أخرى) is a muḍāf ilayhi. The meaning of this speech will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(وإن تدع مثقلة الى حملها لا يحمل منه شيء ولو كان ذا قربى): (إن) is conditional; (تدع) is the protasis; (مثقلة) is an adjective of an omitted agent, i.e. "a burdened soul"; (الى حملها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تدع); the direct object is omitted because it is known; (لا) is negative; (يحمل) is passive and is the apodosis; (منه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an adjective of (شيء); the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (لو) is conditional; (كان) is a defective past verb and its subject (ism) is a latent pronoun whose implied form is "the one called upon (al-madʿū)"; (ذا قربى) is its khabar, meaning "possessor of kinship (qarāba)".
(إنما تنذر الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب وأقامو الصلاة): (إنما) is kāffa and makfūfa (a restricting particle with the particle it restricts); (تنذر) is an imperfect verb and its agent is a latent pronoun, the implied form being "you (anta)"; (الذين) is the direct object; the clause (يخشون) is the ṣila (relative clause); (ربهم) is a direct object; (بالغيب) is a ḥāl from the agent, i.e. they fear their Lord while absent from His punishment, or they fear His punishment while it is absent from them; (وأقاموا الصلاة) is a past verb, an agent and a direct object.
(ومن تزكى يتزكى لنفسه وإلى الله المصير): the wāw is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya), and it is permissible that it be resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); (من) is a jussive-governing conditional noun and a mubtadaʾ; (تزكى) is a past verb in the position of a jussive, the protasis; the fāʾ is the connecting fāʾ of the apodosis; (إنما) is kāffa and makfūfa; (يتزكى) is an imperfect verb and its agent is a latent pronoun whose implied form is "he"; (لنفسه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يتزكى), as a qualification of it; (إلى الله) is a fronted khabar and (المصير) is a postponed mubtadaʾ.

* Rhetoric:
1 - In His saying «أنتم الفقراء الى الله» there is the definite article on (الفقراء). The secret in it is exaggeration of their poverty: as if, because of the intensity of their neediness, they are the ones branded with "the poor", and the neediness of others, compared with their poverty, is not counted as neediness; or as if they have reached the utmost of need and the furthest limit of want, the very genus of the poor. This is among the marvels of the science of bayān.
2 - In His saying «ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى» there is paronomasia of derivation (jinās al-ishtiqāq) among (تزر), (وازرة) and (وزر). Al-wizr, as in al-Miṣbāḥ, is sin, and al-wizr is also a weight; hence it is said wazara yazir, of the pattern waʿada, when one carried a sin. Here a question arises: how does this statement agree with His saying, the Exalted: «وليحملن أثقالاً مع أثقالهم»? The answer is that this verse concerns those who go astray and lead others astray: they carry the burdens of their own misguidance and the burdens of their misleading of others. As for the verse before us, it is restricted to those who carry the sins and burdens of themselves. On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās: the father meets his son, and the two say to him, "O my son, carry for us some of our sins." He says, "I cannot; what is upon me is enough for me."

dervis-irab:19-24.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الحرور): the wording of al-Zamakhsharī: "Al-ḥarūr is the samūm (scorching wind), except that the samūm occurs by day, while the ḥarūr occurs by night and day; and it is said, by day only." And in al-Miṣbāḥ: "Al-ḥarr with fatḥa is the opposite of cold. One says ḥarra the day and the food, yaḥarr, of the pattern taʿiba, and ḥarra ḥarūran, of the patterns ḍaraba and qaʿada, is a dialectal form; the noun is al-ḥarāra"; so it is ḥārr. And ḥarrat al-nār taḥarr, of the pattern taʿiba, means the fire blazed and flared. And al-ḥarra with fatḥa: land with black stones; the plural is ḥirār, like kalba and kilāb. And al-ḥarūr, on the pattern of rasūl, is the hot wind. Al-Farrāʾ said: it occurs by night and by day. Abū ʿUbayda said: Ruʾba informed us that the ḥarūr is by day and the samūm by night. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: the ḥarūr and the samūm are by night and by day, and the ḥarūr is feminine." And the wording of al-Qāmūs: "Al-ḥarūr: the hot wind by night, and it may be by day; and constant heat; and fire."

* I'rab:
(وما يستوي الأعمى والبصير ولا الظلمات ولا النور ولا الظل ولا الحرور): a resumptive speech (kalām mustaʾnaf) conveyed to give an example for the believer and the disbeliever and the incompatibility between them in essence and attribute and what remains in the Hereafter. (ما) is negative; (يستوي) is an imperfect verb which is not satisfied with a single agent, and therefore something must be conjoined to it or it must be multiplied; (الأعمى) is the agent; (البصير) is conjoined to it, and what follows is likewise conjoined; and (لا) is redundant, for emphasis.
(وما يستوي الأحياء والا الأموات إن الله يسمع من يشاء): the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (يستوي الأحياء) is an imperfect verb and an agent; (لا) before (الأموات) is conjoined; (إن) and its subject, and the clause (يسمع) is its khabar; (من) is a relative noun and a direct object; and the clause (يشاء) is the ṣila.
(وما أنت بمسمع من في القبور): the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is the negative Ḥijāzī mā; (أنت) is its subject (ism); (بمسمع): the bāʾ is a redundant preposition and (مسمع) is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar of mā; (من) is the object of (مسمع) because it is an active participle; (في القبور) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, the ṣila of (من).
(إن أنت إلا نذير): (إن) is negative; (أنت) is a mubtadaʾ; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (نذير) is the khabar of (أنت).
(إنا ارسلناك بالحق بشيراً ونذيراً): (إن) and its subject; the clause (أرسلناك) is its khabar; (بالحق) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أرسلناك), and it is said to be in the position of an accusative ḥāl from the agent, i.e. "as those in the right (muḥiqqīn)", or from the object, i.e. "as one in the right (muḥiqqan)", or an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a sending accompanied by the truth"; (بشيراً) is a ḥāl; (ونذيراً) is conjoined to (بشيراً).
(وإن من أمة إلا خلا فيها نذير): the wāw is a conjunction; (إن) is negative; (من) is a redundant preposition and (أمة) is genitive in form and nominative in position as a mubtadaʾ; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; the clause is the khabar of (إن), i.e. "passed (salafa)"; (فيها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (خلا); (نذير) is the agent.

* Rhetoric:
Simile-parable (tamthīl) and antithesis (ṭibāq):
In His saying «الأعمى والبصير» is an example for the believer and the disbeliever, and «والظلمات والنور» is an example for truth and falsehood, and likewise «الظل والحرور»; and «الأحياء والأموات» is an example for those who entered Islam and those who did not enter it and persisted in disbelief. The discussion of tamthīl has already been given in full, and the antithesis present in each of what was mentioned is not hidden.

* Benefits:
The wāw in negation:
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is lā when it is joined with the conjunctive wāw? I say: when the wāw occurs in negation, lā is joined with it to emphasize the meaning of negation."

dervis-irab:25-28.t:
* Vocabulary:
(جُدَدٌ): with ḍamma on the jīm and fatḥa on the dāl; plural of judda, which is a path in a mountain or elsewhere, or it is the streak and the track, from your saying "I cut (jadadtu) the thing", i.e. I cut it. Labīd ibn Rabīʿa said: «أو مذهب جدد على ألواحه» (or a gilded one, with stripes upon its planks). Abū al-Faḍl said: "It is whatever, among the tracks, differs in colour from what adjoins it; from it comes judda of the donkey, for the line on its back." What is meant in the mountains is that which has stripes whose colour differs from the colour of the mountain.
(غَرابِيبُ): plural of gharbīb, which is the black that reaches the extreme of blackness. One says aswad gharbīb and aswad ḥalkūk, which is that which goes far in blackness and is remote in it; from it comes al-ghurāb (the crow). In al-Qāmūs: "aswad gharbīb ḥālik; as for «غرابيب سود», the word (سود) is a badal (substitute), because the emphasis of colours is not put first." More of this discussion will come in the section on I'rab.

* I'rab:
(وَإِنْ يُكَذِّبُوكَ فَقَدْ كَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional; (يكذبوك) is the protasis; the wāw is the agent and the kāf is the direct object; (فقد): the fāʾ is the connecting fāʾ of the apodosis and (قد) is a particle of confirmation; (كذب الذين) is a verb and an agent; (من قبلهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, the ṣila; and the clause (فقد كذب) is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis. It is preferable that the apodosis be omitted, its implied form being "so be patient as they were patient", with His saying (فقد كذب) as evidence for it.
(جاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ وَبِالزُّبُرِ وَبِالْكِتابِ الْمُنِيرِ): the clause (جاءتهم) is a ḥāl; it is a past verb and a direct object; (رسلهم) is the agent; (بالبينات) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (جاءتهم), and what follows is conjoined to it; (المنير) is an adjective of (كتاب). What is meant by (الزبر) is the scrolls of Ibrāhīm, and by «الكتاب المنير» the Torah and the Gospel.
(ثُمَّ أَخَذْتُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَكَيْفَ كانَ نَكِيرِ): (ثم) is a conjunction; (أخذت الذين كفروا) is a verb, an agent and a direct object; the fāʾ is resumptive; (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative, a khabar of (كان) fronted before it; (نكيري) is its subject (ism). The yāʾ was dropped in the script to respect the verse-ending (fāṣila). Al-nakīr has the meaning of al-inkār, i.e. My denunciation of them by punishment and destruction. The interrogative here has the meaning of affirmation (taqrīr), i.e. that it fell in its place and met its proper objects.
(أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً): a resumptive speech conveyed to affirm what preceded of the mention of the differing conditions of people, and that it is a constant matter in all created things. The hamza is for affirmative interrogation; (لم) is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; (تر) is an imperfect verb jussive by (لم) and its agent is a latent pronoun whose implied form is "you"; (أن) and its subject (ism) stand in place of the two objects of (تر); (أن) and its subject, and the clause (أنزل من السماء) is its khabar; (ماء) is the object of (أنزل).
(فَأَخْرَجْنا بِهِ ثَمَراتٍ مُخْتَلِفاً أَلْوانُها): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (أخرجنا) is conjoined to (أنزل) by way of iltifāt (shift) from the third person to the first person; (به) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أخرجنا); (ثمرات) is the object of (أخرجنا); (مختلفا) is an adjective of (ثمرات), and it is a causal adjective (naʿt sababī); (ألوانها) is its agent, and therefore it was not made feminine, because it is attributed to a broken plural in which both masculine and feminine are permissible. The secret of this iltifāt will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(وَمِنَ الْجِبالِ جُدَدٌ بِيضٌ وَحُمْرٌ مُخْتَلِفٌ أَلْوانُها وَغَرابِيبُ سُودٌ): (ومن الجبال): the wāw is resumptive; (من الجبال), the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (جدد) is a postponed mubtadaʾ. The secret of this nominal sentence will come in the section on Rhetoric. (بيض) is an adjective of (جدد); (حمر) is conjoined to (بيض); (مختلف) is also an adjective of (جدد); (ألوانها) is the agent of (مختلف). Its like has preceded, and therefore it is not permissible to parse it as a postponed mubtadaʾ and a fronted khabar, because agreement would then be obligatory. (غرابيب) is conjoined to (جدد) and (سود) is a badal from (غرابيب). Al-Zamakhsharī made it conjoined to (بيض) or to (جدد). He said: "As if it were said: among the mountains is what is streaked, having stripes, and among them is what is of one colour." Then he said: "It is necessary to posit the omission of a muḍāf in His saying «ومن الجبال جدد», meaning 'and among the mountains is what has white, red and black stripes', so that it comes back to your saying 'and among the mountains is what is varied in its colours', as He said «ثمرات مختلفا ألوانها»." After «غرابيب سود» He did not mention "varied in colours" as He mentioned it after white and red, because al-gharbīb is that which reaches the extreme of blackness, so it became a single colour without variation, unlike what preceded.
(وَمِنَ النَّاسِ وَالدَّوَابِّ وَالْأَنْعامِ مُخْتَلِفٌ أَلْوانُهُ كَذلِكَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (من الناس) is a fronted khabar; (الدواب) and (الأنعام) are conjoined to (الناس); (مختلف ألوانه) is an adjective of an omitted element which is the mubtadaʾ, i.e. "a kind varied in its colours among people"; (كذلك) is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar of (مختلف), i.e. "a variation like that".
(إِنَّما يَخْشَى اللَّهَ مِنْ عِبادِهِ الْعُلَماءُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ غَفُورٌ): the sentence is a justification for the seeing, because khashya is knowledge of the One feared and knowledge of His attributes and acts; so whoever is more knowing of Him is more fearful of Him. (إنما) is kāffa and makfūfa; (يخشى الله) is an imperfect verb and a fronted direct object; (من عباده) is a ḥāl; (العلماء) is the agent. The secret of this restriction will come in the section on Rhetoric. (إن) and its subject and its two khabars.

* Rhetoric:
These verses contain lofty arts of bayān, of which we present:
1 - Iltifāt in His saying «فأخرجنا»: He shifted from the third person to the first person because the favour of bringing forth is greater than the sending down of water, and to show the perfection of care for the act, since it contains wondrous workmanship that announces perfect power.
2 - Tadbīj in His saying «ومن الجبال جدد بيض وحمر مختلف ألوانها وغرابيب سود». It has already been given that tadbīj is for the speaker to mention colours intending by them kināya (allusion) and tawriya (double entendre) regarding things, whether description, praise, satire, erotic prelude or other arts. Allah the Exalted intended thereby an allusion to the ambiguous roads, for the white highway is the road much travelled upon, the clearest and most evident of roads, on which the one who strays feels safe and which the one deep in journeys, who is far gone in making the ground of caves his bed, does not fear to cross. For this reason it is said: "He rode with them the white proof, and below it the red, and below the red the black," as though in its concealment and the obscurity of its landmarks it were the opposite of the white in visibility and clarity. Since these three colours are, in visibility to the eye, two extremes and a mean between them (the highest extreme in visibility being whiteness, the lowest extreme in concealment being blackness, and the red between them, by the clarity of colours and compounds), and since the colours of mountains do not, for the most part, go beyond these three colours, and guidance by every sign set up for guidance is divided in this division, the noble verse came in this division, so tadbīj was achieved together with correctness of division. It is laid out in a familiar pattern, conveyed to count the favours with respect to what they guided to: striving to seek benefits and advantages and avoiding worldly and otherworldly perils and destructions.
3 - The turn to the nominal form:
That is in His saying «ومن الجبال»: this sentence and the one after it, «ومن الناس», are brought as nominal sentences, although they share with the verbal sentence before them the use of the content of each of these sentences as evidence for the diversity of people in their conditions. Likewise the difference of mountains, people, beasts and cattle in the colours mentioned is a continuing matter, so it was expressed by what indicates continuity, whereas the bringing forth of various fruits is a newly occurring, renewed matter, so it was expressed by what indicates occurrence.
4 - Fronting, postponing and restriction:
In His saying «إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء»: it restricts khashya to the scholars, as though it were said: those who fear Allah among His servants are the scholars and not others. But if you were to put the agent first, the meaning would be reversed to: they fear none but Allah. These are two different meanings, as is clear to the one who reflects.

dervis-irab:1-3.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فاطِرِ السَّماواتِ): their Creator without a precedent. The root meaning of al-faṭr is splitting in general; it is also said to be splitting lengthwise, and its verb pattern is naṣara, as in al-Mukhtār. From Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās: "I did not know what fāṭir al-samāwāt wa-l-arḍ meant until two Bedouins came to me disputing over a well, and one of them said: 'I faṭartuhā', meaning I began it and originated it." Some have gathered the meanings of this root, despite their differences, saying:
الابتداء والابتداع فطر ... والصّدع والغمز وأما الفطر
فترك صوم بعض كمء فطر ... وما بدا من عنب في الشجر
(Beginning and originating are faṭr, as are cleaving and pressing; as for al-fiṭr, it is giving up the fast, like a mushroom [that bursts forth], and what appears of grapes on the tree.)
(تُؤْفَكُونَ): you are turned away, from al-afk with fatḥa, which is turning away. One says:
"What turned you away (ma afakaka) from such and such?", i.e. what turned you away from it. It is also said to be from al-ifk with kasra, which is lying. In al-Mukhtār: "al-Afk with fatḥa is the maṣdar of afakahu, meaning he overturned him and turned him away from something, and its verb pattern is ḍaraba; from it comes His saying, the Exalted: «قالوا أجئتنا لتأفكنا عما وجدنا عليه آباءنا»."

* I'rab:
(الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ فاطِرِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ) (الحمد) is a mubtadaʾ, (لله) is its khabar, and (فاطر السموات) is a naʿt of it. (الأرض) is conjoined to (السموات). The (أل) in (الحمد) is generic and all-inclusive, i.e. the whole genus of praise. The annexation in (فاطر السموات) is a true annexation (muḥḍa) because it refers to the past. (جاعِلِ الْمَلائِكَةِ رُسُلًا أُولِي أَجْنِحَةٍ مَثْنى وَثُلاثَ وَرُباعَ) (جاعل الملائكة) is a second naʿt, and the annexation here too is a true one. Some regarded it as not true, because it narrates a state; hence it is sound for the active participle to govern, since it does not govern when it has the sense of the past. For this reason some made (رسلا) accusative by an implied verb. Al-Kisāʾī permitted its governing in every case. (رسلا) is the second object of (جاعل). If (جاعل) means "creator", then (رسلا) is an implied ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara). (أولي أجنحة) is a naʿt of (رسلا). (مثنى وثلاث ورباع) are adjectives of (أجنحة), and they are diptotes because of being adjectives and because of deviation from repetition, i.e. two by two, three by three, four by four. The discussion of these adjectives was given earlier in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ. Al-Kāzarūnī in his marginal commentary parsed them as a badal of (أجنحة). (يَزِيدُ فِي الْخَلْقِ ما يَشاءُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) A resumptive statement confirming what precedes. (في الخلق) is attached to (يزيد). (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi and the clause (يشاء) is a ṣila. (إن) with its ism; (على كل شيء) is attached to (قدير); (قدير) is the khabar of (إن); and the clause is causal, with no grammatical position.
(ما يَفْتَحِ اللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ مِنْ رَحْمَةٍ فَلا مُمْسِكَ لَها) (ما) is a jussive conditional noun, in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi of (يفتح). (يفتح) is the fiʿl al-sharṭ and (الله) is the agent. (وللناس) is attached to (يفتح). (ومن رحمة) is a ḥāl. The fāʾ is the linking particle of the apodosis. (لا) is the lā of generic negation, (ممسك) is its ism and (لها) its khabar; the clause is in the position of jussive, the apodosis. (وَما يُمْسِكْ فَلا مُرْسِلَ لَهُ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ) The wāw is a conjunction. (ما) is a jussive conditional noun, likewise in the position of accusative as a fronted object of (يمسك). (يمسك) is the fiʿl al-sharṭ. The fāʾ is the linking particle. (لا) is the lā of generic negation, (مرسل) its ism and (له) its khabar. In His first statement (فلا ممسك لها) the feminine is carried according to the meaning of (ما), because what is meant is mercy; in the second it is carried according to the word. (ومن بعده) is a ḥāl, i.e. after His withholding. (هو) is a mubtadaʾ, (العزيز) is the first khabar and (الحكيم) the second.
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ) (يا) is a vocative particle. (أي) is the one addressed, an indefinite noun made definite by being intended, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative. The hāʾ is for alerting, and (الناس) is a badal. (اذكروا نعمة الله) is an imperative verb with its agent, a mafʿūl bihi and a muḍāf ilayhi. (عليكم) is attached to (نعمة) because it has the sense of "bestowing of favour" (al-inʿām); if it has the sense of "the thing bestowed", the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl.
(هَلْ مِنْ خالِقٍ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ يَرْزُقُكُمْ مِنَ السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ) (هل) is an interrogative particle. (من) is a redundant preposition. (خالق) is a mubtadaʾ, genitive in form and nominative in position. (غير الله) is a naʿt of (خالق) either according to the position or according to the form, or is accusative as an exception; all of these were read. The khabar of (خالق) is omitted, i.e. "for you". It is permissible for the clause (يرزقكم) to be accusative as a ḥāl, or nominative as a naʿt of (خالق) by position, or genitive as a naʿt of (خالق) by form, and it may also be a khabar of (خالق). (ومن السماء) is attached to (يرزقكم), and (الأرض) is conjoined. More on the i'rab of this verse and what was said about it will come in the section on benefits. The meaning of the question is affirmation and rebuke.
(لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَأَنَّى تُؤْفَكُونَ) A resumptive clause given to establish the negation derived from the question. The i'rab of «لا إله إلا الله» has been given in detail before. (فأنى): the fāʾ is resumptive, and (أنى) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. (تؤفكون) is a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the deputy agent.

* Benefits:
1- The meaning of «نزيد في الخلق ما نشاء»:
These verses contain many benefits. The first is the meaning of the addition in creation, and we see that the best of what has been said on it is what al-Zamakhsharī gave in his Kashshāf. After citing what the scholars said, he said: "The verse is unrestricted, and covers every addition in creation: height of stature, symmetry of form, completeness of the limbs, strength in seizing, soundness of intellect, excellence of judgment, boldness of heart, generosity of soul, fluency of tongue, eloquence in speech, good deliberation in handling affairs, and the like, which description cannot encompass." This statement, for all its brevity and eloquence, is comprehensive and exclusive, and contains a satisfying explanation of the differences you see among Allah's creatures.
And He used "opening" metaphorically for releasing and sending, as though they were locked doors that none but Allah opens, of all kinds of blessings and varieties of favours, such as provision, rain, health, security in one's homeland, and other things beyond counting.
The indefiniteness of "mercy" indicates diffusion and vagueness, so that all kinds of blessings are included within it, as stated before.
2- The i'rab of «هل من خالق»:
Some prevented the clause (يرزقكم) from being a khabar of (خالق), because, according to the sounder view, (هل) does not enter upon a mubtadaʾ whose predicate is a verb.
3- Places where «من» is redundant:
We said elsewhere that the prepositional «من» is added before an indefinite noun when preceded by negation, prohibition or a question, and we add here that this is regular in nine positions:
1- At the beginning of a sentence.
2- In the agent.
3- In the ism of kāna.
4- In the object of a verb that takes one object.
5- In the first of the two objects of ظننت.
6- In the first of the objects of علمت.
7- In the first of the two objects of أعطيت.
8- In the second of the two objects of أعطيت.
9- In the object of a verb whose agent is not named (the passive).

dervis-irab:4-7.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِنْ يُكَذِّبُوكَ فَقَدْ كُذِّبَتْ رُسُلٌ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ) A resumptive statement given to console him ﷺ, in that he has a good example in the prophets before him. (إن) is a jussive conditional particle. (يكذبوك) is the fiʿl al-sharṭ, its jussive sign being the omission of the nūn; the wāw is the agent and the kāf is the object. The fāʾ is the linking particle of the apodosis. The clause (قد كذبت) is in the position of jussive, the apodosis; it puts the cause in place of the effect, which is taking comfort, and the implied form is: "so take comfort in the denial of the messengers before you". (رسل) is the nāʾib fāʿil, and (من قبلك) is a naʿt of (رسل). By this implication the objection is answered that it is proper for the consequence to follow the condition, whereas this precedes it.
(وَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الْأُمُورُ) The wāw is a conjunction. (وإلى الله) is attached to (ترجع), and (الأمور) is the nāʾib fāʿil. (يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ) (يا أيها الناس): its i'rab has been given many times. (إن) with its ism and khabar. (فَلا تَغُرَّنَّكُمُ الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا وَلا يَغُرَّنَّكُمْ بِاللَّهِ الْغَرُورُ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the eloquent fāʾ, introducing a consequence of an omitted clause). (لا) is prohibitive. (تغرنكم) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because of its attachment to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and it is in the position of jussive through the prohibitive (لا); the kāf is the object, (الحياة) is the agent, and (الدنيا) is a naʿt. (ولا يغرنكم بالله الغرور) is conjoined to what precedes. (الغرور) with fatḥa on the ghayn is an intensive form like (الصبور) and (الشكور); what is meant by it is Satan, because that is his habit.
(إِنَّ الشَّيْطانَ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ فَاتَّخِذُوهُ عَدُوًّا) (إن) with its ism. (لكم) is attached to (عدو) or is a ḥāl from it, and (عدو) is the khabar of (إن). The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ. (اتخذوه) is an imperative verb with its agent and a first mafʿūl bihi, and (عدوا) is a second mafʿūl bihi.
(إِنَّما يَدْعُوا حِزْبَهُ لِيَكُونُوا مِنْ أَصْحابِ السَّعِيرِ) (إنما) is kāffa and makfūfa. (يدعو) is an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, implied "he", and (حزبه) is a mafʿūl bihi. The lām is causal. (يكونوا) is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied (أن), permissibly, after the causal lām. It is also possible that the lām is the lām of consequence or outcome (ṣayrūra or ʿāqiba). The wāw is the ism of (يكونوا), and (من أصحاب السعير) is its khabar. (الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَهُمْ عَذابٌ شَدِيدٌ) (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (كفروا) is a ṣila. (لهم) is a fronted khabar and (عذاب) is a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the khabar of (الذين). (شديد) is a naʿt. It is permissible for the relative noun to be a badal from the wāw in (ليكونوا), or a naʿt of (حزبه), in which case its position is accusative; it may also be in the position of genitive as a badal of (أصحاب), or a naʿt of (أصحاب). (وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَأَجْرٌ كَبِيرٌ) (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (آمنوا) is a ṣila. (وعملوا الصالحات) is conjoined to (آمنوا). (لهم) is a fronted khabar and (مغفرة) is a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is the khabar of (الذين). (أجر) is conjoined to (مغفرة), and (كبير) is a naʿt.

dervis-irab:29-31.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَتْلُونَ كِتابَ اللَّهِ وَأَقامُوا الصَّلاةَ): (إن) and its subject (ism); the clause (يتلون) is the ṣila (relative clause); (كتاب الله) is the object of (يتلون); (وأقاموا الصلاة) is a past verb, an agent and a direct object, and it is conjoined to the ṣila, entering within its scope.
(وَأَنْفَقُوا مِمَّا رَزَقْناهُمْ سِرًّا وَعَلانِيَةً): also conjoined; (أنفقوا) is a verb and an agent; (مما) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أنفقوا); the clause (رزقناهم) is the ṣila; (سرا) and (علانية) are accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "in secret and in public", and in that is an allusion to spending in whatever way it is made possible. You may also make them accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "secretly and openly". It is also said that it is an allusion to voluntary charity in general, for which the best is that it be in secret, and to zakāt, which can only be public.
(يَرْجُونَ تِجارَةً لَنْ تَبُورَ): the clause (يرجون) is the khabar (predicate) of (إن); (تجارة) is a direct object (mafʿūl bihi); (لن) is a particle of negation, accusative case and futurity; (تبور) is an imperfect verb made accusative by (لن); and the clause (لن تبور) is an adjective (ṣifa) of (تجارة).
(لِيُوَفِّيَهُمْ أُجُورَهُمْ وَيَزِيدَهُمْ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ إِنَّهُ غَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ): the lām is for consequence and becoming (ʿāqiba, ṣayrūra) or for justification; (يوفيهم) is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied (أن) after the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (لن تبور), in the sense that it will never be unsold, so that He may pay them in full the wages of their righteous deeds. It is also said that the lām is attached to an omitted element indicated by the context, i.e. "they did that so that He may pay them in full". The hāʾ is the first object of (يوفيهم) and (أجورهم) is a second direct object; (يزيدهم) is conjoined to (يوفيهم); (إن) and its subject; (غفور) is its first khabar and (شكور) its second khabar; and the clause of inna is a justification of the paying in full and the increase that preceded. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed making the clause (يرجون) in the position of an accusative ḥāl, i.e. "and they spent hoping", with the khabar of (إن) being His saying (إنه غفور شكور).
(وَالَّذِي أَوْحَيْنا إِلَيْكَ مِنَ الْكِتابِ هُوَ الْحَقُّ): (الذي) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (أوحينا) is the ṣila; (إليك) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أوحينا); (من الكتاب) is a ḥāl; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ or a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); (الحق) is the khabar of (هو), and the nominal sentence is the khabar of (الذي); or (الحق) is the khabar of (الذي).
(مُصَدِّقاً لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِعِبادِهِ لَخَبِيرٌ بَصِيرٌ): (مصدقا) is a confirming ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida), i.e. "and in agreement with the Books that preceded it"; (لما) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (مصدقا); the adverbial is attached to an omitted element, the ṣila of (ما); (يديه) is a muḍāf ilayhi, i.e. of the Books that preceded it; (إن) and its subject; (بعباده) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (خبير); the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (خبير) and (بصير) are two khabars of (إن), i.e. knowing of what is apparent and what is hidden in them.

dervis-irab:32-35.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نَصَبٌ): fatigue. In al-Qāmūs: "naṣiba, like fariḥa: he was worn out." And in al-Mukhtār: "naṣiba: he tired, and its pattern is ṭariba."
(لُغُوبٌ): exhaustion from fatigue. In al-Qāmūs: "laghiba, laghaban and laghūban, like manaʿa, samiʿa and karuma: he was exhausted with the severest exhaustion." And in al-Mukhtār: "Al-lughūb, with two ḍammas, is fatigue and exhaustion; its pattern is dakhala; and laghiba with kasra, laghūban, is a weak dialectal form." The apparent sense of what appears in the lexicons is that the two agree in meaning, but al-Zamakhsharī distinguished between them with a fine distinction. He said: "If you say, what is the difference between al-naṣab and al-lughūb? I say: al-naṣab is the fatigue and hardship that befalls the one who is exerting himself on a matter and engaged in it, while al-lughūb is the languor that overtakes him because of the exertion. So al-naṣab is the hardship and strain itself, and al-lughūb is its result and what arises from it of weariness and slackness."

* I'rab:
(ثُمَّ أَوْرَثْنَا الْكِتابَ الَّذِينَ اصْطَفَيْنا مِنْ عِبادِنا): (ثم) is a conjunction of order with delay; (أورثنا الكتاب) is a verb, an agent and a second direct object. The second object was put first only with the aim of honouring and exalting the Book, and its meaning will come in the section on Rhetoric. (الذين) is the first object, and the clause (اصطفينا) is the ṣila of (الذين); (من عبادنا) is a ḥāl.
(فَمِنْهُمْ ظالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ وَمِنْهُمْ مُقْتَصِدٌ وَمِنْهُمْ سابِقٌ بِالْخَيْراتِ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ): the fāʾ is one of ramification (tafrīʿiyya), because He divided His servants to whom He gave the Book as inheritance, as will come. (منهم) is a fronted khabar and (ظالم) is a postponed mubtadaʾ; (لنفسه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ظالم); these are the first division. (ومنهم مقتصد) is conjoined to what precedes, and they are the second division; (ومنهم سابق بالخيرات) is also conjoined, and they are the third division; (بإذن الله) is a ḥāl or is attached to (سابق). The detail of that will come in the section on Benefits.
(ذلِكَ هُوَ الْفَضْلُ الْكَبِيرُ): (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ; (هو) is a second mubtadaʾ or a pronoun of separation; (الفضل الكبير) is the khabar of (هو), and the sentence is the khabar of (ذلك); or (الفضل الكبير) is the khabar of (ذلك).
(جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ يَدْخُلُونَها): (جنات عدن) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يدخلونها) is the khabar. Al-Zamakhsharī parsed it as a badal (substitute) from (الفضل), and there is no obstacle; but al-Zamakhsharī slipped through this parsing into establishing his Muʿtazilite creed, as will come in the section on Benefits, for its curiosity.
(يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيها مِنْ أَساوِرَ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ وَلُؤْلُؤاً وَلِباسُهُمْ فِيها حَرِيرٌ): the sentence is a second khabar. Its parsing has already been given in Sūrat al-Ḥajj, where it occurred in this very wording, so renew your acquaintance with it. It is strange that al-Zamakhsharī, who parsed (لؤلؤا) as accusative by an omitted verb in Sūrat al-Ḥajj, i.e. "and they will be given", parsed it here as conjoined to the position of (من أساور), saying: "(ولؤلؤا) is conjoined to the position of (من أساور), and (من) enters for partitiveness, i.e. they are adorned with some bracelets of gold." (ولباسهم) is a mubtadaʾ, (فيها) is a ḥāl, and (حرير) is the khabar.
(وَقالُوا الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَذْهَبَ عَنَّا الْحَزَنَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (قالوا) is a past verb by which the imperfect is meant, and the turn to the past is to indicate certainty (taḥqīq); (الحمد) is a mubtadaʾ and (لله) is the khabar; (الذي) is an adjective (naʿt); the clause (أذهب عنا) is the ṣila; (الحزن) is the direct object of (أذهب), which became transitive by the hamza; (عنا) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أذهب).
(إِنَّ رَبَّنا لَغَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ): (إن) and its subject; the shifted lām; (غفور) is the first khabar of (إن) and (شكور) the second.
(الَّذِي أَحَلَّنا دارَ الْمُقامَةِ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ): a badal from the preceding (الذي); the clause (أحلنا) is the ṣila, and it is a past verb, a latent agent and a first direct object; (دار المقامة) is a second direct object, i.e. "He lodged us in the abode of residence"; (من فضله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أحلنا), and (من) is for beginning or for justification.
(لا يَمَسُّنا فِيها نَصَبٌ وَلا يَمَسُّنا فِيها لُغُوبٌ): the clause (لا يمسنا) is a ḥāl from the first object of (أحلنا), and it is permissible that it be a ḥāl from the second object, the first being preferable; (يمسنا) is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object; (فيها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يمسنا); (نصب) is the agent; and (ولا يمسنا فيها لغوب) is conjoined to what preceded.

* Rhetoric:
1 - In His saying «ثم أحدثنا الكتاب الذين اصطفينا من عبادنا» [Translator's note: the source prints «أحدثنا» (we brought into being) where the verse reads «أورثنا» (we made inherit), as parsed above] there is a metaphor of the implicit, derivative kind (istiʿāra makniyya tabaʿiyya): the giving of the Book to them, without toil or fatigue in its reaching them, is likened to the bequeathing to an heir.
2 - In this verse there is also the art of "joining with division" (al-jamʿ maʿa al-taqsīm), which is for the speaker to join two or more things in one ruling and then divide what he joined, or to divide first and then join. The first is like the verse mentioned and His saying, the Exalted: «يوم تأتي لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه فمنهم شقي وسعيد» to the end of the verse.

* Benefits:
1 - The order according to the stations of people:
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was the wrongdoer put first, then the moderate, then the foremost? I say: to announce the great number of the transgressors and their predominance, and that the moderate are few in relation to them, and the foremost are fewer than few." Al-Khāzin made this meaning clear in a fuller wording, saying: "If you say: why was the wrongdoer put first, then the moderate, then the foremost? I say: it is said that He ordered them in this order according to the stations of people, because the conditions of people are three: disobedience, heedlessness and repentance. When a man disobeys he enters the sphere of the wrongdoers; when he repents he enters the number of the moderate; and when his repentance is sound and his worship and striving are many, he enters the ranks of the foremost."
2 - Between the Muʿtazila and Ahl al-Sunna:
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: how did you make «جنات عدن» a badal from «الفضل الكبير»? I say: because the pointing to «الفضل» is to the foremost in good deeds, which is the cause of the Gardens and of obtaining reward, so He put the cause in the place of the effect. And in the restricting of the mention of the reward to the foremost, to the exclusion of the others, is what requires caution; so let the moderate be cautious, and let the one who wrongs himself take care, and let both turn to sincere repentance, and not be deceived by what ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, related from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: 'Our foremost is foremost, our moderate is saved, and our wrongdoer is forgiven'; for the condition of that is soundness of repentance, so let him not delude himself with trickery." This speech runs on the school of the Muʿtazila; as for Ahl al-Sunna, they permit forgiveness by mere grace. Ibn al-Munayyir said in refutation of al-Zamakhsharī: "This verse opened with the mention of those chosen from Allah's servants, then divided them into the wrongdoer, the moderate and the foremost, so that it necessarily follows that the one who wrongs himself among the monotheists is included among the chosen and is one of them. And what blessing is more complete and greater than His choosing for tawḥīd and for creeds free of innovations? What then is the matter with the author (that is, al-Zamakhsharī) that he goes on at length in equating the chosen monotheist with the audacious disbeliever?"
A glimpse of the Muʿtazila:
The Muʿtazila are a sect of the Muslims who hold that acts of good are from Allah and acts of evil are from man; that Allah the Exalted is obliged to consider what is best for His servants; that the Qur'an is originated and created, not eternal; that Allah the Exalted will not be seen on the Day of Resurrection; that the believer who commits a major sin is in a station between the two stations, meaning that he is neither a believer nor a disbeliever; that whoever enters the Fire does not leave it; that faith is speech, action and belief; that the inimitability of the Qur'an lies in the turning away (of the Arabs) from it, not that it is in itself inimitable, and that had the Arabs not been turned away from opposing it they would have brought something to oppose it; that the non-existent is a thing; that good and evil are rationally known; and that Allah the Exalted is living by His essence, not by life, knowing by His essence, not by knowledge, and powerful by His essence, not by power.
Among the famous and notable Muʿtazila are al-Jāḥiẓ, Abū al-Hudhayl al-ʿAllāf, Ibrāhīm al-Naẓẓām, Wāṣil ibn ʿAṭāʾ, Aḥmad ibn Ḥābiṭ, Bishr ibn al-Muʿtamir, Maʿmar ibn ʿAbbād al-Sulamī, Abū Mūsā ʿĪsā nicknamed al-Muzdār and known as the monk of the Muʿtazila, Thumāma ibn Ashras, Hishām ibn ʿAmr al-Fuwaṭī, Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Abī ʿAmr al-Khayyāṭ and the teacher al-Kaʿbī, Abū ʿAlī al-Jubbāʾī, teacher of Shaykh Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī at first, and his son Abū Hāshim ʿAbd al-Salām. These are the heads of the school of iʿtizāl. Most of the Shāfiʿīs are Ashʿarīs; most of the Ḥanafīs are Muʿtazila; most of the Mālikīs are Qadarīs; and most of the Ḥanbalīs are Ḥashwiyya. Among the Muʿtazila are Abū al-Qāsim al-Ṣāḥib Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbbād, al-Zamakhsharī, al-Farrāʾ the grammarian, and al-Sīrāfī. [Translator's note: this closing list is reproduced as printed in the source; several of the attributions are questionable.]

dervis-irab:36-38.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَصْطَرِخُونَ): they cry out to one another (يتصارخون); of the form (يفتعلون) from al-ṣurākh, which is shouting with effort and hardship. Al-Aʿshā said:
قصدت إلى عنس لأحدج رحلها ... وقد حان من تلك الديار رحيلها
فأنّت كما أنّ الأسير وصرخت ... كصرخة حبلى أسلمتها قبيلها
(I made for a she-camel to saddle her litter, when the time of departure from those dwellings had come. She groaned as the captive groans, and cried out like the cry of a pregnant woman whom her women attendants have abandoned.)
That is: she groaned like the groaning of a captive in the first, and raised her voice in the second, like the cry of a woman in labour whom her qabīl, those who serve her at birth, have left. Al-qabīl, al-qabūl and al-qābila are she who attends to the woman's need at childbirth and receives the child when it comes out. As for verbs beginning with one of the letters of iṭbāq, namely ṣād, ḍād, ṭāʾ and ẓāʾ, when the form (افتعل) and what is conjugated from it is made from them, the tāʾ of ifti'āl is replaced by ṭāʾ. Example: the verbs صلح, ضرب, طرد, ظلم: when we build the form (افتعل) from them we say, by analogy, اصتلح, اضترب, اطترد, اظتلم; and to lighten the pronunciation the tāʾ is replaced by ṭāʾ, the similarity between them being evident, so they are changed to اصطلح, اضطرب, اطرد, اظطلم. For a word like اظطلم two further forms are permissible: اظّلم and اطّلم. [Translator's note: the third item, اطرد, is printed so in the source; the expected form would be اطّرد.]

* I'rab:
(وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَهُمْ نارُ جَهَنَّمَ): conjoined to His saying «إن الذين يتلون كتاب الله»; (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila (relative clause); (لهم) is a fronted khabar (predicate); (نار جهنم) is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and the nominal sentence is the khabar of (الذين).
(لا يُقْضى عَلَيْهِمْ فَيَمُوتُوا وَلا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمْ مِنْ عَذابِها): the sentence is a second khabar of (الذين) or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from them; (لا) is negative; (يقضى) is a passive imperfect verb, i.e. death is not decreed against them; (عليهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يقضى); the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation (sababiyya); (يموتوا) is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied (أن) after the fāʾ of causation; (ولا يخفف) is conjoined to (لا يقضى); (عنهم) may stand in place of the agent (deputy agent, nāʾib fāʿil), and (من عذابها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يخفف), and the reverse is permissible.
(كَذلِكَ نَجْزِي كُلَّ كَفُورٍ): (كذلك) is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); (نجزي) is an imperfect verb with a latent agent; (كل كفور) is a direct object.
(وَهُمْ يَصْطَرِخُونَ فِيها رَبَّنا أَخْرِجْنا نَعْمَلْ صالِحاً غَيْرَ الَّذِي كُنَّا نَعْمَلُ): the wāw is a conjunction; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يصطرخون) is the khabar; (فيها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يصطرخون); (ربنا) is a vocative muḍāf from which the particle of vocative is omitted; the vocative clause and what follows it is the quoted speech of an omitted verb of saying, in the position of an accusative ḥāl, i.e. "saying, 'Our Lord'"; (أخرجنا) is an imperative verb with the meaning of supplication, its agent latent and (نا) the object; (نعمل) is an imperfect verb jussive because it is the response to the imperative (jawāb al-amr), its agent latent, the implied form being "we"; (صالحا غير الذي): the two may be adjectives of an omitted maṣdar or of an omitted direct object, and it is also permissible that (صالحا) be an adjective of the maṣdar while (غير الذي) is the object; the clause (كنا) is the ṣila of the relative; (كان) and its subject, and the clause (نعمل) is the khabar of (كنا).
(أَوَلَمْ نُعَمِّرْكُمْ ما يَتَذَكَّرُ فِيهِ مَنْ تَذَكَّرَ): the sentence is the quoted speech of an omitted verb of saying, i.e. "It will be said to them: 'Did We not grant you life...'". The hamza is for interrogation of denunciation and rebuke, and the wāw is a conjunction to an implied clause, i.e. "Did We not give you respite and delay you for a lifetime in which whoever would be reminded could be reminded", that is a time that afforded you reflection had it occurred to you to reflect; (لم) is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; (نعمركم) is an imperfect verb jussive by (لم), its agent latent, the implied form being "We", and the kāf is a direct object; (ما) is a specific indefinite (nakira maqṣūda) meaning "a time", so it is in the position of an accusative adverb of time, or of a maṣdar, i.e. "a lifespan"; the clause (يتذكر) is an adjective of (ما); (فيه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يتذكر); (من) is the agent, and the clause (تذكر) is the ṣila.
(وَجاءَكُمُ النَّذِيرُ فَذُوقُوا فَما لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ نَصِيرٍ): the wāw is a conjunction; the clause (جاءكم النذير) is conjoined to (أولم نعمركم), because its wording is a wording of inquiry while its meaning is a meaning of report, as if it were said, "We granted you life and the warner came to you". (فذوقوا): the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ (fāʾ faṣīḥa), for ordering the command to taste upon what precedes it of the granting of life and the coming of the warner; the fāʾ in (فما) is for justification; (ما) is negative; (للظالمين) is a fronted khabar; (من) is a redundant preposition and (نصير) is a postponed mubtadaʾ, in position nominative though genitive in form by (من). It is permissible that (ما) be Ḥijāzī according to those who allow the fronting of its khabar before its subject.
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ عالِمُ غَيْبِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): (إن) and its subject; (عالم) is its khabar and what follows is a muḍāf ilayhi. (إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذاتِ الصُّدُورِ): (إن) and its subject; (عليم) is its khabar; (بذات الصدور) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (عليم). The discussion of (ذات) has already been given at length.

dervis-irab:8-8.t:
* I'rab:
(أَفَمَنْ زُيِّنَ لَهُ سُوءُ عَمَلِهِ فَرَآهُ حَسَناً فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يُضِلُّ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَهْدِي مَنْ يَشاءُ) A resumptive statement given to confirm the preceding contrast between the outcomes of the two groups by explaining the contrast between their states, which leads to those two outcomes.
The hamza is for a rhetorical question of denial. The fāʾ is a conjunction joined to an omitted clause; parallels of this have already been given. (من) is a relative noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, as the context indicates; the implied form is "like him whom Allah has guided". Badr al-Dīn ibn Mālik parsed it as a conditional noun whose apodosis is omitted, its implied form being: "your soul would go out in regret over them". The clause (زين) is a ṣila of (من). (وله) is attached to (زين), and (سوء عمله) is the nāʾib fāʿil. (فرآه): the fāʾ is a conjunction, (رآه) is conjoined to (زين), the hāʾ is the first object of (رأى) and (حسنا) is its second object, since it is a verb of the heart. The fāʾ is the linking particle because of the sense of condition in the relative noun. (إن) with its ism, and the clause (يضل) is its khabar. (من يشاء) is the object of (يضل). The clause (ويهدي من يشاء) is conjoined to the clause (يضل من يشاء). (فَلا تَذْهَبْ نَفْسُكَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَسَراتٍ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِما يَصْنَعُونَ)
The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ. (لا) is prohibitive. (تذهب) is an imperfect verb, jussive through (لا). (نفسك) is the agent. (عليهم) is attached to (تذهب), as you say "he perished for love of him" and "he died of grief over him". It is not permissible for it to be attached to (حسرات), because the ṣila of a maṣdar is not placed before it. (حسرات) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), the meaning being: "do not destroy yourself out of regrets". Al-Mubarrad said it is a tamyīz (specification). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may be a ḥāl, as if the whole of him had turned into regrets because of excessive regret, as Jarīr said:
مشق الهواجر لحمهن مع السرى ... حتى ذهبن كلا كلا وصدورا
(The midday heat and night travel stripped their flesh until they became mere breastbones and chests.)
He is describing she-camels as emaciated. One says faras mamshūq, meaning a tall, lean horse, and jāriya mamshūqat al-qawām, a slender girl. Al-hājira is the intensity of heat; al-surā, with ḍamma, is night travel; al-kalkal and al-kalkāl are the chest. That is, from the intensity of the heat they became as though only bones, with no flesh on them. The conjoining of (الصدور) to (الكلاكل) is for explanation. More on this topic will come in the chapter on rhetoric.
(إن) with its ism and khabar, and (بما يصنعون) is attached to (عليم).

* Rhetoric:
In His words: «فلا تذهب نفسك عليهم حسرات» there is the art of īghāl, which is bringing words that serve as a precautionary completion of what preceded. Allah the Exalted swore by the life of the Messenger more than once that those who turned away from him and opposed him had exceeded every limit by their turning away, and He showed that they were excessive in dullness and deep in error, as He said the Exalted in more than one place: «لعمرك انهم لفي سكرتهم يعمهون», and also His words: «ولا يحزنك الذين يسارعون في الكفر», and His words: «فلعلك باخع نفسك على آثارهم إن لم يؤمنوا بهذا الحديث أسفا». The going out of the soul in regret and sorrow is a distinguished expression which poets have often watched, and an ancient poet said:
فعلى إثرهم تساقط نفسي ... حسرات وذكرهم لي سقام
(After them my soul falls away in regrets, and the remembrance of them is a sickness to me.)
When grief struck him after the departure of his loved ones, took hold of his soul and mastered his blood, he imagined it scattering and falling from his body in successive regrets. He made the soul into regrets because of their mingling, as though it were they; or it falls away after them because of regrets and griefs. "Their remembrance", that is, remembering them, "is a sickness (saqām) to me", saqām with fatḥa being a maṣdar like saqam. Ibn al-Rūmī borrowed this fine expression in lamenting his son Muḥammad, the middle of his children:
وظل على الأيدي تساقط نفسه ... ويذوي كما يذوي القضيب من الزند
(He remained on the hands as his soul fell away piece by piece, and he withered as a twig withers from the fire-stick.)
A sick person is carried on the hands only if he is small; his son Muḥammad died in a haemorrhage, at an age between four and five.
I say: history reports that this verse was revealed concerning Abū Jahl ibn Hishām, when the evil of his deed was made attractive to him and he saw it as right or beautiful, and so wandered in error, "releasing the one who commands prohibition" and embracing obedience to desire, until he saw the beautiful as ugly and the ugly as beautiful, as though rust had covered him and stripped him of his reason, intellect and discernment. Abū Nuwās watched the sky of this meaning and said:
اسقني حتى تراني ... حسنا عندي القبيح
(Give me drink until you see me regard the ugly as beautiful.)
He says to the wine-server: give me drink until I am drunk and the ugly becomes beautiful to me. (حسنا) is the second object of (تراني), and (القبيح) is the agent of (حسنا) because it is an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha).
«[Translator's note: the phrase "وأطلق آمر النهي" is translated literally as "released the one who commands prohibition"; its sense is unclear in the source.]»

dervis-irab:9-10.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بَلَدٍ): In al-Miṣbāḥ: "al-balad is masculine or feminine", and al-balda is al-balad. Both al-balad and al-balda are applied to every place on the earth, whether inhabited or empty. In the Revelation: «إلى بلد ميت», that is, to a land with no vegetation or pasture, which is then brought forth by the rain and grazed by their livestock; so death was applied to the absence of vegetation and pasture, and life to their presence."
(الْكَلِمُ): a generic noun (ism jins), because it denotes the essence as such; it is not a plural, contrary to the author of al-Qāmūs and other grammarians, because its pronoun may be masculine whereas a plural tends to take the feminine; nor is it a collective noun (ism jamʿ), because it has a singular from its own wording, whereas the usual case with a collective noun is otherwise. Its singular is kalima, and kalima has three dialectal forms: kalima with fatḥa on the kāf and kasra on the lām, kilma with kasra on the kāf and sukūn on the lām, and kalma with fatḥa on the kāf and sukūn on the lām.
(يَبُورُ): perishes and is ruined. One says bāra yabūru būran wa-bawāran: it perished. Al-sūq or al-silʿa bārat means it stagnated; bāra al-ʿamal means the work became void; bārat al-arḍ means the land was not sown; bawwara al-arḍ means he left it or made it barren; abārahu means he destroyed him; tabawwara nafsahu means he mourned for himself and wailed from destruction. Al-bāʾir is land that has lain fallow, and the plural is būr. One says ḥāʾir bāʾir, meaning one who obeys no guide and heads nowhere. Al-būr is also the corrupt, ruined one in whom there is no good; one says imraʾa būr and qawm būr. Al-būr of land is what has not been sown; al-bawār is destruction and ruin; and dār al-bawār is Hell.

* I'rab:
(وَاللَّهُ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ الرِّياحَ فَتُثِيرُ سَحاباً) (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and (الذي) is its khabar. The clause (أرسل الرياح) is the ṣila of the relative noun, and (الرياح) is a mafʿūl bihi. The fāʾ is a conjunction. (تثير) is an imperfect verb; the secret of conjoining an imperfect to a past verb, and how it comes differing from what precedes and follows it, will come in the chapter on rhetoric. (سحابا) is a mafʿūl bihi. (فَسُقْناهُ إِلى بَلَدٍ مَيِّتٍ فَأَحْيَيْنا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِها كَذلِكَ النُّشُورُ) (فسقناه) is also a conjunction, in the manner of iltifāt (shift of person). (سقناه) is a verb with its agent and object. (وإلى بلد) is attached to (سقناه), and (ميت) is a naʿt. (فأحيينا به الأرض) is also a conjunction, and the adverbial phrase is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (كذلك) is a fronted khabar and (النشور) is a postponed mubtadaʾ; the secret of this simile will come in the chapter on rhetoric. (مَنْ كانَ يُرِيدُ الْعِزَّةَ فَلِلَّهِ الْعِزَّةُ جَمِيعاً) (من) is a jussive conditional noun, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ. (كان) is a defective past verb whose ism is a latent pronoun referring back to (من), and the clause (يريد) is its khabar. (العزة) is a mafʿūl bihi. The fāʾ is the linking particle of the apodosis. (لله) is a fronted khabar and (العزة) a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is in the position of jussive, the apodosis. It was sound for this clause to stand in place of the apodosis because it indicates it, since a thing is sought only from its possessor and owner. A parallel is your saying "whoever wants good advice, it is with the righteous", meaning "let him seek it with them", except that you put what indicates it in its place. The meaning of «فلله العزة جميعا» is that all might belongs exclusively to Allah. Others said: "(من) is conditional, a mubtadaʾ, and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being 'let him give Him' (فليعطه); and His words «فلله العزة» are the reason for the omitted apodosis." Al-Bayḍāwī gave the omitted apodosis as "let him obey Him" (فليطعه). (لله) is a fronted khabar, (العزة) a postponed mubtadaʾ and (جميعا) a ḥāl. The conditional clause with its apodosis is the khabar of (من).
(إِلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ الْكَلِمُ الطَّيِّبُ وَالْعَمَلُ الصَّالِحُ يَرْفَعُهُ) The clause is accusative as a ḥāl. (إليه) is attached to (يصعد). (يصعد الكلم) is an imperfect verb and its agent, and (الطيب) is a naʿt of (الكلم). (والعمل) is a mubtadaʾ; its being nominative by conjunction is also permissible. (الصالح) is a naʿt, and the clause (يرفعه) is the khabar of (العمل). The agent of (يرفعه) is a latent pronoun referring back to (العمل), i.e. the good deed raises the good word. It is also said that the agent is the pronoun of Allah, in which case the hāʾ refers back to (العمل). From Ibn al-Muqaffaʿ: "A word without deed is like tharīd without fat, a cloud without rain, and a bow without a string." (وَالَّذِينَ يَمْكُرُونَ السَّيِّئاتِ لَهُمْ عَذابٌ شَدِيدٌ وَمَكْرُ أُولئِكَ هُوَ يَبُورُ) A resumptive statement given to explain the state of the evil word and the bad deed, after explaining the state of the good word and the righteous deed and their people. (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يمكرون) is the ṣila of (الذين). (السيئات) is a naʿt of a mafʿūl muṭlaq, the implied form being "the evil plottings" (al-makarāt al-sayyiʾāt); it is not permissible to make it accusative as a mafʿūl bihi, because (مكر) is an intransitive verb. Al-makarāt, with fatḥas, is the plural of makra, with sukūn on the kāf, which is a single instance of makr, meaning scheme and deception. Some said it is permissible to give (يمكرون السيئات) the meaning of (يكسبون السيئات) ("they earn evil deeds"), in which case it may be accusative as a mafʿūl bihi. (مكر) is a mubtadaʾ and (أولئك) is a muḍāf ilayhi. The demonstrative was placed where the pronoun would be, to signal that they are distinguished by evil and corruption from all other wrongdoers, i.e. they and no others. (هو) is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl), with no grammatical position, and the clause (يبور) is the khabar of (مكر). It is also possible that (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يبور) its khabar, the nominal clause being the khabar of (مكر). There is disagreement about the occurrence of the separating pronoun before a khabar: some prevented it and others allowed it, and we incline to permissibility.

* Rhetoric:
1- Iltifāt (shift):
In His words «والله الذي أرسل الرياح فتثير سحابا فسقناه إلخ» there are two shifts. The first is in reporting the past with an imperfect: He said «فتثير» in the imperfect, while what precedes and follows it is past, to narrate a past state and to bring that fine picture before the mind, indicating the perfection of power and wisdom. This is done with every action that has a kind of distinction or specificity, such as a state that is strange or that concerns the addressee, and the like, as Taʾabbaṭa Sharrā said:
فمن ينكر وجود الغول إني ... أخبر عن يقين بل عيان
(Whoever denies the existence of the ghoul, I report from certainty, indeed from eyewitness,)
بأني قد لقيت الغول تهوي ... بسهب كالصحيفة صحصحان
(That I met the ghoul rushing down on a plain like a sheet, level and wide,)
فأضربها بلا دهش فخرت ... صريعا لليدين وللجران
(And I struck her without dismay and she fell, prostrate on her hands and her neck.)
Al-ghūl is the female of the devils; al-ʿiyān is seeing with the eye; al-hawī is descending, and what is meant is speed of running; al-sahb, with fatḥa, is open space level and distant at its edges; al-ṣaḥīfa is the book; al-ṣaḥṣaḥān, with fatḥa, is level ground; and al-jirān, like kitāb, is the front of the neck bone from the throat to the upper chest, with plurals jurun and ajrina. He says: whoever denies the existence of the ghoul has lied, for I report from certainty; or the meaning: O you who deny the existence of the ghoul, I report a report arising from certainty, which is what rests on decisive proof, let alone eyewitness with the eye.
In this style is what came in the report of al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām at the battle of Badr. He said: "I met ʿUbayda ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ on a horse, in full armour so that nothing was seen of him but his eyes, and he was saying: 'I am Abū Dhāt al-Kurūsh.' I had a short spear in my hand and I thrust (fa-aṭʿunu) with it into his eye, and he fell, and I trod (waʾaṭaʾu) with my foot on his cheek until the spear came out bent." His words «فأطعن بها في عينه وأطأ برجلي» are turned from the past wording to the imperfect, to portray to the listener the scene in which he did what he did of daring and boldness in killing that armoured horseman. Do you not see that he first said "I met ʿUbayda" in the past, and then said "and I thrust with it into his eye"? Had he conjoined his speech to its beginning, he would have said "so I thrust (faṭaʿantu) with it into his eye".
The second shift is in His words: «فسقناه إلى بلد ميت فأحيينا إلخ». Had it followed the pattern of the discourse, He would have said "so he drove ... and he revived", but He turned from the third-person wording to the first-person wording, which is more fitting for specification and indicates it more strongly. He expressed with two pasts after the imperfect to indicate certainty of occurrence.
2- Simile:
In His words «كذلك النشور» there is a simile mursal (with the particle stated), because the particle is present; that is, as the reviving of dead land, so is the resurrection of the dead, in the soundness of its being within power or in the manner of the reviving.
3- Figurative attribution (majāz isnādī):
In His words «إليه يصعد الكلم الطيب والعمل الصالح يرفعه» there is figurative usage in the predicate and in the attribution. Ascent is figurative for knowledge, because ascent is a quality of bodies, and the word is known; so the verb was attributed to the object.

dervis-irab:11-14.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فُراتٌ): extremely sweet. In al-Qāmūs: "farata al-māʾ, like karuma, furūtatan: it was sweet."
(أُجاجٌ): extremely salty. In al-Qāmūs: "ajja al-māʾ ujūjan, with ḍamma, ya'ujju like yasmaʿu, yaḍribu and yanṣuru, when its saltiness is intense." You say hajīr ujāj of the sun, in which there is majāj, which is the saliva of the sun; and māʾ ujāj burns with its saltiness.
(قِطْمِيرٍ): al-qiṭmīr is the wrapping of the date stone, which is the thin skin wound around it; it is also said to be the speck on its back. It is known that the date stone has four things which are used as proverbs for smallness: al-fatīl, which is what is in the cleft of the stone; al-qiṭmīr, which is the wrapping; al-naqīr, which is what is on its back; and al-thufrūq, which is between the cap and the stone. Al-Jawharī said: "It is said to be the white speck on the back of the stone from which the palm grows."

* I'rab:
(وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ تُرابٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ جَعَلَكُمْ أَزْواجاً) A resumptive statement given to bring another confirmation or another proof of the soundness of resurrection and revival. (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (خلقكم) is its khabar. (ومن تراب) is attached to (خلقكم). (ثم) is a conjunction of sequence with delay. (ومن نطفة) is conjoined to (من تراب). (ثم جعلكم أزواجا) is conjoined to (خلقكم من تراب), and (أزواجا) is the second object of (جعل), i.e. kinds, males and females.
(وَما تَحْمِلُ مِنْ أُنْثى وَلا تَضَعُ إِلَّا بِعِلْمِهِ) The wāw is a conjunction. (ما) is negative. (تحمل) is an imperfect verb, nominative. (من) is a redundant preposition and (أنثى) is genitive through (من) in form and nominative in position as the agent. (ولا تضع) is conjoined to (وما تحمل). (إلا) is a particle of restriction, and (بعلمه) is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. known to Him. «[Translator's note: the printed text has a stray "ز" before the next sentence.]» (وما يعمر من معمر ولا ينقص من عمره إلا في كتاب) The wāw is a conjunction. (ما) is negative. (يعمر) is a passive imperfect verb. (من) is a redundant preposition and (معمر) is the nāʾib fāʿil. (ولا ينقص) is conjoined to (وما يعمر). «من» («of his life") is attached to (ينقص). (إلا) is a particle of restriction, and (في كتاب) is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. The meaning of this indulgent expression will come in the chapter on rhetoric. (إن ذلك على الله يسير) (إن) with its ism; (على الله) is attached to (يسير); (يسير) is the khabar of (إن). In al-Miṣbāḥ: "yasura al-shayʾ, like qaruba, means it was little, so it is yasīr al-amr; yaysiru yusran, of the pattern taʿiba, and yasura yusran, of the pattern qaruba, so it is yasīr, that is, easy; Allah made it easy (yassarahu) and it became easy (tayassara), and istaysara has the same meaning."
(وما يستوى البحران هذا عذب فرات سائغ شرابه وهذا ملح أجاج) A resumptive statement given to coin a parable for the believer and the disbeliever. (ما) is negative. (يستوي) is an imperfect verb, nominative. (البحران) is the agent, nominative, its sign of nominative being the alif, being a dual. (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ, (عذب) is a khabar and (فرات) is a second khabar or a naʿt. (سائغ شرابه): (سائغ) may be a third naʿt, with (شرابه) as agent of (سائغ) because it is an assimilated adjective, i.e. its drink goes down easily. It is also possible that (سائغ) is a fronted khabar and (شرابه) a postponed mubtadaʾ, the clause being a second naʿt. The clause (هذا عذب إلخ) is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from (البحران). (وهذا ملح أجاج) is conjoined to (عذب فرات). More elaboration on this parable will come in the chapter on rhetoric.
(ومن كل تأكلون لحماً طرياً وتستخرجون حلية تلبسونها) The wāw is either a conjunction, the clause then serving as a completion of the parable, or resumptive, the clause then being a resumptive digression (istiṭrād). The detail of each of the two meanings will come in the chapter on rhetoric. (ومن كل) is attached to (تأكلون), and (منهما) is a naʿt of the omitted noun after (كل), i.e. each one of them. (تأكلون) is an imperfect verb with its agent, and (لحما) is a mafʿūl bihi; (طريا) is a naʿt. (وتستخرجون) is conjoined to (تأكلون), and (حلية) is a mafʿūl bihi. The clause (تلبسونها) is a naʿt of (حلية). «[Translator's note: the printed text here reads "لحماًََ مفعول به ولحماً مفعول به" with a repeated phrase and "تلبسوننا نعت لحية"; these are evident misprints for (لحما) and (حلية)/(تلبسونها) and are rendered according to their evident sense.]»
(وترى الفلك فيه مواخر لتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون) The wāw is a conjunction. (ترى) is an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, implied "you", and (الفلك) is a mafʿūl bihi. (فيه) is attached to (مواخر), a ḥāl, since the seeing is visual. The lām in (لتبتغوا) is causal, and (تبتغوا) is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied (أن) after the causal lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (مواخر). (ومن فضله) is attached to (تبتغوا). (لعل) with its ism, and the clause (تشكرون) is its khabar.
(يولج الليل في النهار ويولج النهار في الليل) You may take it as resumptive, and you may take it as in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of (خلقكم), i.e. Allah the Exalted. (الليل) is a mafʿūl bihi of (يولج), and (في النهار) is attached to (يولج). (ويولج النهار في الليل) is conjoined to the clause before it. (وسخر الشمس والقمر كل يجري لأجل مسمى) The wāw is a conjunction; the secret of the difference between the two conjoined elements will come in the chapter on rhetoric. (سخر) is a verb whose agent is a latent pronoun referring back to Allah, and (الشمس) is a mafʿūl bihi. (والقمر) is conjoined to (الشمس). (كل) is a mubtadaʾ, i.e. each one of them, and the clause (يجري) is the khabar. (لأجل) is attached to (يجري), and (مسمى) is a naʿt of (أجل). (ذلكم الله ربكم له الملك) (ذلكم) is a mubtadaʾ, and three khabars are given for it: (الله), (ربكم), and the clause (له الملك). (له) is a fronted khabar and (الملك) is a postponed mubtadaʾ. (والذين تدعون من دونه ما يملكون من قمطير) The wāw is circumstantial or resumptive. (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ, the clause (تدعون) is a ṣila, and (من دونه) is a ḥāl. (ما) is negative, (يملكون) is an imperfect verb with its agent, and the clause (ما يملكون) is the khabar of (الذين). (من) is a redundant preposition and (قطمير) is genitive in form, accusative in position as a mafʿūl bihi.
(إن تدعوهم لا يسمعوا دعاءكم ولو سمعوا ما استجابوا لكم) A resumptive statement given to confirm the preceding content. (إن) is a jussive conditional particle. (تدعوهم) is a verb, and the wāw is the agent. «[Translator's note: the source calls (تدعوهم) a past verb ("فعل ماض"); it is in fact an imperfect verb, jussive.]» (ما) is negative. (استجابوا) is a verb with its agent, and the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the answer to a non-jussive condition. (ويوم القيامة يكفرون بشرككم) The adverbial is attached to (يكفرون), and (بشرككم) is attached to (يكفرون). The kāf is annexed to the maṣdar, as a maṣdar annexed to its agent, i.e. they will disown you and your worship of them. (ولا ينبئك مثل خبير) The better view is that the address is general, i.e. O listener, whoever you may be. (لا) is negative, (ينبئك) is an imperfect verb with the kāf as its object, and (مثل خبير) is its agent, i.e. one who knows the inner reality of things.

* Rhetoric:
1- Indulgent speech (al-kalām al-mutasāmiḥ):
In His words «وما يعمر من معمر إلخ» there is the art of indulgent speech, in which the speaker trusts the understanding and taste of his listeners, because it will not be confused for them and the grasping of its implications and the comprehension of its aims will not elude them. The apparent wording suggests that the two conjoined elements alternate upon every person and that lengthening of life and its opposite succeed each other upon him, which is impossible in itself; but it is among the self-evident matters grasped at first glance. The common speech of people is on this model; they say: "He does not reward a servant or punish him except justly", and "I did not enjoy a land or dislike it except that my yearning for it lessened." Al-Zamakhsharī says there is also another interpretation, namely that no human's life is lengthened or shortened except in a Book, and its form is that it is written on the Tablet: "If so-and-so performs the pilgrimage, his life is forty years; if he performs the pilgrimage and fights, his life is sixty years." If both are combined and he reaches sixty, he has been granted a long life; if only one is done and he does not pass forty, then some of his life, whose limit is sixty, has been reduced.
2- Parable (al-tamthīl):
In His words «وما يستوي البحران إلخ» — some call it the extended metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya) — it is a construction used in other than its original place because of a relation of similarity, in which neither the thing likened nor the particle of likening is mentioned. An example that clarifies it is their saying: "You are striking cold iron." He likened the state of one who persists in obtaining something that cannot be achieved to the state of one who strikes cold iron, on the basis that each is work behind which no result is hoped. There is no mention of the thing likened nor of the particle of likening in this construction, so it is an extended metaphor, because it is a construction used for other than what it was set for, and the similarity between the figurative and the literal meanings is evident. This type is frequent in current proverbs, prose and verse, such as their saying: "If you were a wind, you have met a hurricane", said to one who lords it over you, or to a strong person who falls upon one stronger and fiercer than he; yet the addressee was not a wind and did not meet a hurricane.
ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī has a delightful passage on tamthīl, which we summarise as follows. He said: "Can it be doubted that it works the work of magic, so that what lies between East and West is shortened?" And he said: "It shows you, for the meanings represented in the imagination, likenesses in matching persons; it makes the mute speak for you and gives you eloquence from the inarticulate; it shows you life in the inanimate and shows you the reconciliation of opposites, and makes the distant thing near."
In Asrār al-Balāgha ʿAbd al-Qāhir cited a splendid poetic example. He said: "Consider likewise the verse of Abū Tammām:
وإذا أراد الله نشر فضيلة ... طويت أتاح لها لسان حسود
(When Allah wills to spread a virtue that has been folded away, He gives it the tongue of an envier.)
taken apart from the verse that follows it, although the verse is clear in meaning; then follow it with the next verse, which is:
لولا اشتعال النار فيما جاورت ... ما كان يعرف طيب عرف العود
(Were it not for the fire's blazing in what it neighbours, the sweet fragrance of aloes-wood would not be known.)
And see whether the meaning displayed the full beauty of its dress and revealed the hidden part of its loveliness and adornment, and deserved all its precedence, except through the last verse and the tamthīl and imagery in it."
Not every simile, however, turns into a metaphor, as the preceding discussion might suggest; this is allowed only when the likeness between the two things is one whose grasp is near and easy of reach, and there is in the situation an indication of it, so that the addressee, when the name is applied to him freely, can know what you meant. If there is no way to know the intended likeness except after mentioning the sentences by which the parable is tied, metaphor does not enter it, because when the likeness is obscure it is not permitted to take the name by force and transfer it to what is its proper bearer without a witness accompanying you that points to the likeness. ʿAbd al-Qāhir illustrated this with a verse by al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī. He said: "If you tried to turn the poet's words:
فإنك كالليل الذي هو مدركي ... وإن خلت أن المنتأى عنك واسع
(For you are like the night that will overtake me, even if I thought the place of refuge from you was wide)
into a metaphor, and treat the night as you treat the lion in your saying 'I saw a lion', you would find no way for it in speech, because you would be left with one of two things: either you omit the qualification and confine yourself to mentioning the night alone, saying 'if I flee, the night shades me', which is absurd, since there is nothing in the night to indicate the point the poet intended, that he will not escape him however far he flees, because of the breadth of his dominion and the length of his reach; or, if you do not omit the qualification, you find that the way of metaphor in it leads to strain; for were you to say 'if I flee from you I find a night that overtakes me, though I thought the place of refuge was wide and the flight far', you would say what natures do not accept, because custom has not applied it to the one praised in this way."
Let us return to the verse we are discussing. Allah gave the believer and the disbeliever the parable of the two seas, and then favoured the salty sea over the disbeliever in that it shares with the sweet in benefits, from fish, pearls, and the running of ships with what benefits people, whereas the disbeliever is devoid of benefit. This is in the manner of His words the Exalted: «ثم قست قلوبكم من بعد ذلك فهي كالحجارة أو أشد قسوة» and then He said: «وإن من الحجارة لما يتفجر منه الأنهار وإن منها لما يشقق فيخرج منه الماء وإن منها لما يهبط من خشية الله». It is also said that the believer and the disbeliever, though they share some qualities such as courage and generosity, are not equal in the greatest distinguishing feature, because one of them remains on his original nature.
«[Translator's note: the source quotes 2:74 as «ثم قسمت قلوبكم…», «لما يتفجر من الأنهار» and «وان لما يهبط»; these are misprints for the text of the Qur'an and are given here in the standard form.]»
3- Digression (al-istiṭrād):
Since digression has been mentioned, we say that it was referred to earlier in this book and here we add to its exposition. It is that a poet or writer builds much speech upon speech of another kind, interrupts it while it is his real aim, apart from all that preceded, and returns to his first speech. Most of what comes is by way of simile. In the verse there is a digression to the mention of the two seas, the salty and the sweet, and the bounty and gift attached to them: from each of them you eat fresh meat, which is fish, and extract ornaments to wear: the ring is placed on the finger, the bracelet on the wrist, the necklace on the neck and the anklet on the leg. And you see the ships in each of them mawākhir, that is, cleaving the water as they run through it. One says makharat al-safīna al-māʾ, and clouds are called banāt makhr because they cleave (tamkhuru) the air; and al-safn, from which safīna is derived, is close to al-makhr, because it scrapes the water as though peeling it, as it cleaves it.

dervis-irab:39-40.t:
* Vocabulary:
(خَلائِفَ): plural of khalīfa, i.e. some of you succeed others.
