The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: "The one made a successor is called khalīfa and khalīf; the plural of khalīfa is khalāʾif and that of khalīf is khulafāʾ." No root has been found that is distributed over as many meanings as this one, and whoever consults it in the lexicons sees wonders; for this reason some scholars gathered its meanings in these verses:
عديم خير حدّ سيف خلف ... والاستقا والقرن أما الخلف
فاسم لعشب الصيف ثم الخلف ... للوعد ليس من صفات الحر
ذهاب شهوة الطعام خلفه ... ورقعة ونبت صيف خلفه
كذا اختلاف الوحش ثم الخلفة ... اسم إلى العيب وذاك يزري
الولد الصالح هذاك خلف ... وجمع خلفة لرقعة خلف
وخلفة بالضم جمعها خلف ... لعنب وذاك أصل الخمر
(Roughly: one devoid of good; the edge of a sword; drawing water; the horn; as for al-khalaf it is the name of summer herbage; then al-khulf is breaking a promise, which is no attribute of a free man; loss of appetite for food; a patch; summer growth; likewise the going back and forth of wild animals; then al-khilfa is a name for a defect, which disgraces; the righteous child is khalaf; and the plural of khilfa, for a patch, is khalaf; and khulfa with ḍamma has the plural khalaf, for grapes, which is the origin of wine.) [Translator's note: the verses are obscure and the gloss is only a general rendering of their contents.]

* I'rab:
(هُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَكُمْ خَلائِفَ فِي الْأَرْضِ): a resumptive speech (kalām mustaʾnaf) conveyed to explain the conditions of the disbelievers who denied the favour of Allah upon them after He made them successors on the earth. (هو) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (الذي) is its khabar (predicate); the clause (جعلكم) is the ṣila (relative clause); (جعلكم) is a verb, an agent and a first direct object; (خلائف) is a second direct object; (في الأرض) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (خلائف) or to an omitted element that is an adjective of it.
(فَمَنْ كَفَرَ فَعَلَيْهِ كُفْرُهُ وَلا يَزِيدُ الْكافِرِينَ كُفْرُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ إِلَّا مَقْتاً): the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ (fāʾ faṣīḥa); (من) is a jussive-governing conditional noun and a mubtadaʾ; (كفر) is a past verb in the position of a jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ is the connecting fāʾ; (عليه) is a fronted khabar and (كفره) is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the nominal sentence is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is negative; (يزيد الكافرين كفرهم) is an imperfect verb, a fronted direct object and a postponed agent; (عند ربهم) is an adverb of place attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (مقتا) is a second direct object or a tamyīz (specification).
(وَلا يَزِيدُ الْكافِرِينَ كُفْرُهُمْ إِلَّا خَساراً): conjoined to the preceding clause, and repeated for emphasis and for additional affirmation of the firmness of disbelief in their souls and of disbelief's entailing each of the two dreadful things, namely abhorrence and loss.
(قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ شُرَكاءَكُمُ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ): regarding (أرأيتم), it has been said before that it has the meaning of "inform me", and seeing here takes two objects, as will come; it is also said that the interrogative here is a real one and the word does not include the meaning "inform me". (رأيتم) is a verb and an agent; (شركاءكم) is the first direct object of (رأيتم); (الذين) is an adjective; the clause (تدعون) is the ṣila; (من دون الله) is a ḥāl.
(أَرُونِي ماذا خَلَقُوا مِنَ الْأَرْضِ): (أروني) is an imperative verb, an agent and a direct object, and the command is meant as a challenge to show incapacity; the clause is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya). Al-Zamakhsharī parsed it as a badal (substitute) from (أرأيتم), and Abū Ḥayyān answered him with what this space does not allow. The clause (ماذا خلقوا) is in the position of an accusative as a second direct object, either of (رأيتم) or of (أروني), so the matter is one of contention (tanāzuʿ); or the clause (أروني) is parenthetical and (ماذا) admits the two well-known possibilities; or the clause (أروني) is a badal from the clause (أرأيتم), as if it were said, "Inform me about your partners; show me what part they created." (من الأرض) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (خلقوا).
(أَمْ لَهُمْ شِرْكٌ فِي السَّماواتِ): (أم) is a conjunction and it is the disconnected kind (munqaṭiʿa), so it has the meaning of (بل): he has turned away from the first question and begun another. The question is one of denial. (لهم) is a fronted khabar, (شرك) a postponed mubtadaʾ, and (في السموات) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (شرك), i.e. a partnership.
(أَمْ آتَيْناهُمْ كِتاباً فَهُمْ عَلى بَيِّنَةٍ مِنْهُ): conjoined to what preceded; (آتيناهم) is a verb, an agent and a first direct object; (كتابا) is a second direct object; the fāʾ is a conjunction; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ; (على بينة) is the khabar; (منه) is an adjective of (بينة).
(بَلْ إِنْ يَعِدُ الظَّالِمُونَ بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضاً إِلَّا غُرُوراً): (إن) is negative; (يعد الظالمون) is an imperfect verb and an agent; (بعضهم) is a badal from (الظالمون), a part-of-whole substitute; (بعضا) is the object of (يعد); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (غرورا) is accusative by removal of the preposition or is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "except a false promise", and that is by their saying that the idols intercede for us with Allah.

dervis-irab:41-43.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُمْسِكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ أَنْ تَزُولا): (إن) and its subject (ism), and the clause (يمسك السموات والأرض) is its khabar (predicate). (أن تزولا): (أن) and what is within its scope are in the position of an accusative mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "for fear that they should pass away". It is also said that (يمسك) includes the meaning of "prevents", so that (أن) and what is within its scope are in the position of an accusative as a second direct object, or by removal of the preposition, i.e. "from their passing away", the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (يمسك); al-Zajjāj said this. It is also said that (أن) and what is within its scope are in the position of an accusative badal ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) from (السموات), i.e. "He holds their passing away [back]".
(وَلَئِنْ زالَتا إِنْ أَمْسَكَهُما مِنْ أَحَدٍ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ): the wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the lām that prepares for an oath; (إن) is conditional; (زالتا) is a past verb in the position of a jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (إن) is negative; (أمسكهما) is a past verb and a direct object; (من) is a redundant preposition and (أحد) is genitive in form, the agent of (أمسكهما) in position; (من بعده) is a ḥāl or an adjective of (أحد). On the first, the meaning is "after His holding"; on the second, the meaning is "other than Him", i.e. any one other than Him. The clause (إن أمسكهما) has no grammatical position, because it is the answer to the oath, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what is stated, as in his saying in al-Khulāṣa:
واحذف لدى اجتماع شرط وقسم ... جواب ما أخرت فهو ملتزم
(When a condition and an oath come together, omit the answer to whichever you put later; that is obligatory.)
(إِنَّهُ كانَ حَلِيماً غَفُوراً): (إن) and its subject; the clause (كان) is its khabar; (حليما) is the khabar of (كان) and (غفورا) a second khabar.
(وَأَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمانِهِمْ لَئِنْ جاءَهُمْ نَذِيرٌ لَيَكُونُنَّ أَهْدى مِنْ إِحْدَى الْأُمَمِ): (أقسموا) is a verb and an agent; (بالله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أقسموا); (جهد أيمانهم) is accusative as a maṣdar or as a ḥāl, i.e. "striving". Al-Farrāʾ said: "Al-jahd with fatḥa is from your saying 'exert your effort (ijhad jahdaka)', i.e. reach your limit, and al-juhd with ḍamma is capacity; and according to others than al-Farrāʾ both mean capacity." The lām occurs in the answer to the oath; (إن) is conditional; (جاءهم نذير) is a verb, a direct object and an agent; the lām is also an answer to the oath; (يكونن) is an imperfect verb, nominative because it is not directly attached to the nūn of emphasis; its origin is (ليكونونن), one of the nūns was dropped to avoid a succession of similar letters, and when two quiescent letters met the wāw was dropped, the ḍamma remaining as evidence of it; so it is nominative by the persistence of the nūn dropped because of the succession of similar letters, and the dropped wāw is its subject (ism); (أهدى) is its khabar; (من إحدى الأمم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أهدى), i.e. than every one of them.
(فَلَمَّا جاءَهُمْ نَذِيرٌ ما زادَهُمْ إِلَّا نُفُوراً): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (لما) is a temporal adverb (ẓarfiyya ḥīniyya) or a connective that includes the meaning of a condition; (جاءهم نذير) is a verb, a direct object and an agent; the clause (ما زادهم) is the answer to (لما) and has no grammatical position. Al-Shihāb al-Ḥalabī said: "In it is evidence that it, that is lammā, is a particle and not an adverb, since what follows the negative mā does not act upon what precedes it." (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (نفورا) is a second direct object or a tamyīz (specification).
(اسْتِكْباراً فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَكْرَ السَّيِّئِ): (استكبارا) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, i.e. for the sake of arrogance, or a badal from (نفورا), or a ḥāl, i.e. "being arrogant"; (في الأرض) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (استكبارا); (ومكر السيّء) is conjoined to (استكبارا) or to (نفورا), and it is of the construction of the described attached to its description, the original being "the evil plot (al-makr al-sayyiʾ)", or there is an omitted described noun, i.e. "the plot of evil action".
(وَلا يَحِيقُ الْمَكْرُ السَّيِّئُ إِلَّا بِأَهْلِهِ): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (لا) is negative; (يحيق المكر) is an imperfect verb and an agent; (السيّء) is its adjective; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (بأهله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يحيق).
(فَهَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا سُنَّتَ الْأَوَّلِينَ فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَحْوِيلًا): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (هل) is an interrogative particle; (ينظرون) is an imperfect verb and an agent, i.e. they await; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (سنة الأولين) is a direct object. Sunna is a maṣdar sometimes annexed to its object, as here, and at other times to its agent, as in His saying «فلن تجد لسنة الله», because He the Exalted instituted it for them, so its annexation to the agent and to the object is both sound. (لن) is a particle of negation, accusative case and futurity; (تجد) is an imperfect verb made accusative by (لن); (لسنة الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تبديلا); (تبديلا) is the object of (تجد).

* Rhetoric:
1 - Harmony of word with meaning (i'tilāf al-lafẓ maʿa al-maʿnā):
In His saying «وأقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم» is the art of the harmony of word with meaning, namely that the words of the intended meaning agree with one another, with no word among them that is alien to its fellows and unfit for its place, or described as being a good neighbour, so that if the meaning is rare and pure, its words are purely rare, and conversely. Since all the words adjoining the oath in this verse are of common, current usage, no rare word came in it that would need the neighbourhood of what matches it in rarity. This discussion has already been given in full detail in Sūrat Yūsuf.
2 - Proverb-sending (irsāl al-mathal):
In His saying «ولا يحيق المكر السيء إلا بأهله» is the art of irsāl al-mathal. Reference to this art has been made before with many examples, especially in the poetry of Abū al-Ṭayyib, and it is clear here because plotting falls only on its own people. Among their proverbs: "Whoever digs a pit of perdition falls into it." He said in al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "The people fell into aghwiya, i.e. into a calamity; and al-mughawwayāt, with doubled wāw and fatḥa, is the plural of al-mughwāt, which is a pit like the zubya (a pit dug to trap a lion). It is said: whoever digs mughawwayāt falls into them." Kaʿb said to Ibn ʿAbbās: "In the Torah: whoever digs a pit for his brother falls into it." Ibn ʿAbbās said to him: "We found this in the Book of Allah: «ولا يحيق المكر السيء إلا بأهله»."
3 - Figurative attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī):
In His saying «ما زادهم إلا نفورا» is a figurative attribution, because the attribution of increase to the warner is a free metaphor (majāz mursal), since he is a cause of that.

dervis-irab:44-45.t:
* I'rab:
(أَوَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَيَنْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ): a speech conveyed to cite as evidence the running of His, the Exalted, custom in punishing the deniers. The hamza is for interrogation of denial and the wāw is a conjunction to an implied clause that the context requires, i.e. "Did they cling to their dwellings and not travel?" (لم) is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; (يسيروا) is an imperfect verb jussive by (لم), and the wāw is the agent; (في الأرض) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يسيروا); (فينظروا): the fāʾ is a conjunction and (ينظروا) is conjoined to (يسيروا); (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative, the fronted khabar (predicate) of (كان); (عاقبة) is its postponed subject (ism); the sentence is in the position of an accusative as the object of (ينظروا); (الذين) is a muḍāf ilayhi and (من قبلهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of (الذين).
(وَكانُوا أَشَدَّ مِنْهُمْ قُوَّةً): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (كانوا) is (كان) and its subject; (أشد) is its khabar; (منهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أشد); (قوة) is a tamyīz (specification); and the sentence is in the position of an accusative ḥāl (circumstantial).
(وَما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيُعْجِزَهُ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فِي السَّماواتِ وَلا فِي الْأَرْضِ): the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (كان) and its subject; the lām is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd); (يعجزه) is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied (أن) after the lām of denial; the hāʾ is a direct object; (من) is a redundant preposition and (شيء) is genitive in form and nominative in position as the agent of (شيء) [Translator's note: the source reads "the agent of (شيء)", evidently meaning the agent of (يعجزه)]; (في السموات) is an adjective of (شيء); (ولا في الأرض) is conjoined to (في السموات).
(إِنَّهُ كانَ عَلِيماً قَدِيراً): (إن) and its subject; the clause (كان) is its khabar; the subject of (كان) is a latent pronoun, the implied form being "He"; (عليما) and (قديرا) are its two khabars.
(وَلَوْ يُؤاخِذُ اللَّهُ النَّاسَ بِما كَسَبُوا ما تَرَكَ عَلى ظَهْرِها مِنْ دَابَّةٍ): the wāw is a conjunction; (لو) is conditional; (يؤاخذ الله الناس) is an imperfect verb, an agent and a direct object; (بما) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يؤاخذ); (ما) is a relative or a maṣdar particle, i.e. "by what they earned" or "by their earning"; either way the clause (كسبوا) has no grammatical position, and the clause (ما ترك) has no grammatical position because it is the answer to a non-jussive condition; (على ظهرها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ترك); (من) is a redundant preposition and (دابة) is genitive in form and accusative in position as the object of (ترك).
(وَلكِنْ يُؤَخِّرُهُمْ إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى فَإِذا جاءَ أَجَلُهُمْ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ بِعِبادِهِ بَصِيراً): the wāw is a conjunction; (لكن) is the lightened, non-operative one, for rectification (istidrāk); (يؤخرهم) is an imperfect verb, a direct object and a latent agent; (الى أجل) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يؤخرهم); (مسمى) is an adjective (naʿt) of (أجل); (فإذا): the fāʾ is a conjunction and (إذا) is a future adverb; the clause (جاء أجلهم) is in the position of a genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; the answer of (إذا), in which it operates, is omitted, its implied form being "so He will requite them"; the fāʾ is the connecting fāʾ; (إن) and its subject; the clause (كان) is its khabar; (بعباده) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (بصيرا); (بصيرا) is the khabar of (كان).

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «ما ترك على ظهرها إلخ» there is an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya): He likened the earth to the beast on which a person rides, then omitted the likened-to, which is the beast, and left something of its attributes, which is the back. Shaykh-zāda [Translator's note: the source prints «ولزاده», evidently a garbled form of the name of this author, whose gloss on al-Bayḍāwī is meant] has in his gloss on al-Bayḍāwī a subtle question, which we present in his own words. He said: "If it is said: how can the part of the earth on which creatures live be called both the face of the earth and the back of the earth, when the back is the opposite of the face, so that it is a case of applying two opposites to one thing? I say: it is sound by two considerations. Its surface is called the back of the earth in that the earth is like the beast carrying burdens, and it is called the face of the earth because the visible part of it is like the face of an animal, while the other part, like the belly, is what is hidden of it."
